description:
FILED s470bs-merge (Opus, 2026-09-06) while attributing the sweep's movers.
PRE-EXISTING; #1033 only made it VISIBLE.

THE SHAPE.  On Linux `open F, '.'` succeeds (O_RDONLY on a directory is
legal) and every READ from it fails with EISDIR.  perl reports that:

    $ cd /a/dir/with/no/t
    $ perl -e 'my $d = -d "t"; print "errno-after-filetest=", $!+0, "\n";
               open F, "." and binmode F and sysread F, $_, 1;
               print "err=", $!+0, "\n"'
    errno-after-filetest=2
    err=21                      # EISDIR, from the sysread

PCL on the same program (measured on this tree AND on a `git archive 48d8e39`
extraction of main):

    HEAD (with #1033):  errno-after-filetest=2   err=2     <- stale, from the filetest
    48d8e39 (before):   errno-after-filetest=0   err=0

So the filetest half is RIGHT now (#1033); the read half sets no errno at all,
so `$!` keeps whatever the previous op left.  `readline` has the same hole:
`$! = 0; open F, "." and $_ = <F>` leaves `$!` at 0 where perl says 21.

WHY IT COSTS ROWS.  perl-tests/readline.t:66 computes
`open F, '.' and binmode F and sysread F, $_, 1; my $err = $! + 0;` and then
SKIPS its two directory rows unless `$err`.  Before #1033 `$err` was 0 (the
BEGIN block's `-d 't'` set nothing and the sysread set nothing), so the two
rows were SKIPPED -- a coverage hole that read as green.  With #1033 the
`-d 't'` correctly leaves ENOENT behind, `$err` is 2, the block RUNS, and both
rows fail on `$! == $err` because the readline sets no errno either.  Measured
serially on both trees: readline.t 23 pass / 5 fail / 4 skip -> 23 / 7 / 2.
The two rows are blessed in baselines/fail-baseline.tsv with this number.

THE FIX (not attempted here -- it is a read-path change in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp
right after s470br rewrote the handle layer, and it owes the io/ + op/
companion legs).  Both read entries must fail with EISDIR when the underlying
file is a directory: `%p-sysread-impl` and the `%p-read-record` path behind
`p-readline`.  The discriminating measurement is one `fstat` on the handle's
descriptor (S_ISDIR) at open time, remembered on the handle, so neither read
pays a syscall per call.  ACCEPTANCE: the probe above prints err=21 on both
lines, and perl-tests/readline.t rows 12/13 pass (23/7 -> 25/5), which is also
how the two blessed rows leave the baseline.

Probe file: scratch/s470bs/p26.pl (and p25.pl for the open/binmode/sysread
verdicts, which already agree with perl).

=== DONE (s470bx, 2026-09-06) ===

FIXED, and the task's diagnosis was right about the mechanism but short by two
entries: `sysread`/`read`/`readline` set no errno, and `getc` and `eof` did not
merely answer wrongly â they KILLED THE PROGRAM.

On Linux `open F, '.'` SUCCEEDS (O_RDONLY on a directory is legal) and every
read from the handle then fails.  perl answers undef (or an empty record) AND
sets `$!`; PCL answered only the first half, so `$!` kept whatever the previous
operation had left.

  * NEW `%p-read-fail (stream &optional errno)` fstats the descriptor ON THE
    FAILURE PATH and, when it is a directory, sets `$!` through the existing
    `%p-io-errno-fail`.  Deliberately not a per-handle flag (nothing to keep in
    step with dups and reopens, nothing paid on the happy path) and not a
    re-read of the C errno, which s470bs ruled out: an allocation between the
    failing call and the read can clobber it.  Any other read failure leaves
    `$!` alone â what PCL did for all of them before â rather than inventing a
    number perl does not report.
  * `%p-read-impl`'s error arm and `%p-read-record`'s two arms call it (EISDIR).
  * `%p-getc-impl` gained a `handler-case`: it had NONE, so `getc` on a
    directory handle reached SBCL's unhandled `simple-stream-error` and took
    the whole program with it.  EBADF, not EISDIR â perl's getc is the one
    entry of the family that does not report the directory; it takes its
    "handle is not open for reading" exit, whose SETERRNO is EBADF.
  * `%p-eof-impl` gained one too, and it was found only because the probe row
    after `getc` finally got to run: `eof($h)` reached the same unhandled error
    through `peek-char`.  perl answers 1 â a read it cannot perform reads as
    EOF, the rule its closed-handle branch already had â and leaves `$!` at 0,
    so this one is deliberately NOT a `%p-read-fail` call.
  * Both new handlers re-raise `p-exception` the way `%p-read-impl` does (rule
    11): a perl-level die passing through is the caller's, not a read failure.

MEASURED, with `$!` cleared AFTER the open (perl's own open leaves ENOTTY
behind from its isatty() probe, and a sloppy probe reads that instead):
sysread/read/readline/slurp = undef + EISDIR (21); getc = undef + EBADF (9);
eof = 1 + errno untouched.  scratch/s470bx/p1237.pl and p1237b.pl are byte-
identical to perl 5.40.3 except `$!` after a SUCCESSFUL readline, where perl
shows its own open's ENOTTY leftover and PCL shows 0 â perl's own docs say `$!`
after a successful call is undefined.  BEFORE, on a `git archive fcf076f1`
extraction: rows 1-4 answer errno=0 where perl says 21, and the program DIES at
row 5.

ROWS: perl-tests/readline.t 23/7 -> 25/5.  Rows 12 `readline( DIRECTORY )` and
13 `readline( DIRECTORY ) slurp mode`, blessed on this bug by s470bs, leave
`baselines/fail-baseline.tsv` BY EDIT; `baselines/pass-baseline.tsv` moves with
them (TOTAL 18647 -> 18649).  `baselines/row-shortfall.tsv`'s cause for that
file named #1237 and was WRONG: its six unproduced rows are the file's early
stop at test 32, not this bug â corrected in passing.

The COMPANION population moves the same way and back onto a snapshot it had
silently fallen behind: t/op/readline.t C 23/9 on the base extraction against a
blessed snapshot of 25/7, and 25/7 here with ROW DIFF 0/0/0/0.  t/op/read.t
2116/0 and t/io/fs.t 59/2 unchanged on both trees.

GUARD: `Pl/t/errno-01.t` +9 rows (19 -> 28), every expectation the output of
the SAME program under perl, run inside the test rather than written down â
the errnos differ per entry and a hand-copied table would be a second source.
Inverse-verified on the `fcf076f1` extraction: all 9 fail there, the last three
because the program is already dead.

BARS: gate 215 files / 7460 rows, FAIL = the 13 standing pclxs xs rows only
(`use-require-01.t` row 66 died in the #1338 shared-cache prune race and is
70/70 alone).  Full sweep `--jobs 4`: GATE clean, 0 new / 0 fixed, drops 5 =
census, shortfall +0, TOTAL passing 18649 (+2, exactly the rows moved).
Runtime only: no `Pl/` file, no emission change, no generation bump.

FILED #1292 from a probe: a `<...>` GLOB whose interpolation yields THREE OR
MORE pieces emits an N-ARY call to the BINARY `p-.`, so `</etc/$h*>` dies at
LOAD and the program never starts.  PRE-EXISTING at fcf076f1.
subject: `sysread`/`readline` on a DIRECTORY handle does not fail: perl sets $! = EISDIR (21) and returns undef, PCL returns undef with $! untouched.  Exposed (not caused) by #1033: perl-tests/readline.t rows 12/13 used to SKIP on `$err == 0` and now run and fail.
